AC-2 An already-imported or conflicting candidate cannot be selected, and selecting its cluster parent skips it (test).
AC-3 The list header reports the found count and the already-added count (frontend test).
AC-4 The import path's own RD-5 refusal is unchanged (existing tests green).
AC-5 The registry is consulted once per read, not once per candidate (test); eleven-module build, service/persistence/architecture/frontend tests, privacy gate and contract_authority_status green.

report.objective: Show the operator, before they select anything, which discovery candidates are already in the product. Today the already-imported check runs only inside the import path, so a run against an estate whose cluster is already enrolled presents those members as freshly selectable and the operator finds out only after pressing Import. Product Owner directive 2026-09-14: a candidate that is already added appears greyed out and cannot be selected, and the list says how many of the found candidates that is.
output_contract: A discovery result that tells the operator, before selection, what is already in the product.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A read-path join, a selection rule and a screen affordance against existing contracts and an existing repository method.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every new field and method names the clause it serves (14F section 2/3, import contract RD-n, DI-n).

Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. Do not run the full Python pytest suite. Eleven Gradle subprojects. No migration is expected; if one is genuinely needed it is additive at the next free number and sets the audit context before any row it writes.
RD-4 name-blindness: the match is by stable identifier only, never by display name or address.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
Open the PR at the end; do not merge. SESSION_CLOSE names the field, the batch method, the frontend affordance and the test counts before and after.
risks: Freezing the mark at run time so a device added afterwards still looks new.
One registry query per candidate on a forty-row list.
Overwriting import_outcome with a read-time observation.
Letting a cluster selection silently re-import members that already exist.

in: Read path: when the run and its candidates are read, resolve each candidate's match key against the device registry through the existing DeviceDiscoveryMatchRepository (add a batch lookup method rather than calling it per candidate in a loop) and add to the candidate's JSON a field naming its existing state -- new, already_imported, or conflicting per RD-5 -- plus the existing device id when it is already imported. Do not overwrite the persisted import_outcome column with it: that column records what an import did; this field records what the registry says right now. Name them distinctly and say which is which in the SESSION_CLOSE.

Selection rule: a candidate whose existing state is already_imported is not selectable; one that is conflicting is not selectable either and carries its reason. RD-1 still holds: selecting a cluster selects its importable members, and now it must skip the already-imported ones rather than including them. A run where every member is already imported leaves the cluster row visible and selectable-but-empty -- render that honestly rather than hiding the row (DI-3).

Import path: keep its own RD-5 check exactly as it is. The read-path marking is an affordance, not the authority; a candidate that became imported between the read and the import must still be refused per row by the import path, with its outcome.

Frontend: an already-imported row renders greyed out and non-selectable with a short badge naming the state, and the summary line above the table reports the counts, in the shape 'N candidates found, M already added' (and a separate count for conflicting when any exist). A tooltip or secondary line on the row names the existing device so the operator can find it. No role-conditional rendering.

Tests: service tests for the read path (a candidate matching an enrolled device is marked already_imported with its device id; one matching nothing is new; a conflicting match is marked and not selectable), a batch-lookup test proving one query rather than N, a frontend test that the row is disabled and the counts render, and an existing-behaviour test that the import path still refuses per row.
out: Changing the match key or the RD-5 semantics; hiding any candidate; the discovery run itself, the worker, or any device contact; the inventory or configuration screens.

completed: AC-1: DiscoveryRunService.read() now computes a read-time RD-5 projection (CandidateRegistryState: new/already_imported/conflicting + existing device id) per candidate, via a batch registry lookup, exposed as ReadOutcome.Found.registryStateByCandidateId.

AC-5: DeviceDiscoveryMatchRepository.findByDiscoveryMatchKeys(Collection<String>) added (one query for the whole candidate set); implemented in JooqDeviceDiscoveryMatchRepository with a single dynamic IN-clause query; DiscoveryRunService calls it exactly once per read().
DiscoveryController: GET /discovery/runs/{run_id} candidate JSON now carries registry_state and existing_device_id, distinct from the untouched, persisted import_outcome field.

AC-2: frontend AddDeviceDialog.tsx isSelectable() gates single-row and cluster-parent selection so an already_imported/conflicting candidate cannot be selected and a cluster selection skips such members; an all-already-imported cluster stays visible, selectable-but-empty (DI-3), never hidden.

AC-3: frontend summary line above the candidate table renders 'N candidates found, M already added' plus a conflicting count when any exist; an already-imported/conflicting row is greyed out with a badge and, when known, the existing device id.

Import path (DiscoveryRunService.importSelection/importOneCandidate) refactored to share the RD-5 comparison (registryStateFor) with the read path, with its own RD-5 refusal behavior otherwise unchanged.

Tests: 3 new DiscoveryRunServiceTest cases (AC-1 read-time marking incl. device added after the run, conflicting marking, AC-5 single-batch-query assertion) and 1 new AddDeviceDialog.test.tsx case (disabled row + header counts); all pre-existing import-path and cluster-selection tests left green and unmodified (AC-4).
